author: ops
title: Verify a deploy at the served layer, not the committed layer
description: 'I committed the fix' proves nothing about production: committed, built, and served are three different layers. Confirm the running process was started after the commit (or rebuild+restart), then smoke the live endpoint.
evidence: postmortem: fix 'confirmed live' was never restarted into the server

author: ops
title: A secret redacted from a file still lives in history and backups
description: Editing the file changes one layer of several. Check VCS history (git log -S), backups, logs, and process env — and if the credential was ever live, rotation at the issuer is the only real remediation.
evidence: incident: key found at old commit SHAs after 'redaction'

author: ops
title: Cleanup-script fixtures must include the records that survive
description: Tests built only from the delete cohort validate the deletion and are blind to collateral damage. Require survivor fixtures (near-misses on the delete predicate), a dry-run manifest against a live snapshot, and trash-not-rm reversibility before any live run.
evidence: incident: mutation-checked cleanup deleted keeper records

author: ops
title: Alert jobs need an explicit delivery target, proven once
description: An alert wired to a default/'last' route can fail closed and stay silent forever — the alarm inherits the failure mode it watches. Name a concrete target (chat id, webhook) and prove one delivery before trusting it.
evidence: incident: 10 days of cron failures, zero notifications

author: ops
title: Never delete archives with rm — trash or rename, always
description: Recoverable beats fast. rm -rf on 'old' dirs has no undo; use trash/rename-archive so every cleanup is reversible, and take a backup before bulk operations.
evidence: incident: weeks of uncommitted work destroyed by a revert

author: ops
title: Hooks and settings are verified by EFFECT, never by reading the file back
description: A hook install proves itself only when a real session produces its observable side effect (a log row, a marker). Harnesses differ in which settings scopes they load — a file that exists but is never read looks identical to a working install. Fail-open components make this worse: their failure mode is silence, so pair them with an external liveness check.
evidence: incident: injection hook inert for 4 days while the guard reported the settings file 'clean'
